methodology: Read all 540 canonical species JSON at the installation snapshot, all 1282 Master Plant Pool rows, and recursive Git tree metadata.
Accepted-name matches use scientific_name (fallback genus/species/rank); normalization ignores punctuation/case and treats ssp. as subsp.

Alias matches use canonical synonyms[], removing botanical authority suffixes and deduplicating matches to the same canonical ID. These are project representation mappings, not a new independent botanical review of all 56 synonyms.

Reviewed uninstalled candidates are wording-based leads from existing scientific review/status/name notes. They are NOT all verified distinct taxa or READY authorization. Some require accepted-name destinations, range HOLD preservation, or duplicate checks.
Identity triage pending means distinct-versus-alias not yet resolved. It is NOT a genuine botanical identity conflict. One explicit identity conflict was detected: Celtis ehrenbergiana.

Physical coverage counts a nonempty Git tree blob referenced by local images[].file. This does not certify licensing, exact taxon, decoding, or live loading for every historic photo. 432 is a file-presence census, not globally verified one-photo coverage.
Missing local references also exist on species with another usable file; preserve them for targeted repair.
Raw source names/data and all native-range decisions remain untouched. Source snapshot below is the read-only pre-sync view; batch status synchronization is separately recorded.

rows.source_taxonomy_review: Reviewed 2026-10-07 | TAXONOMY+DIAGNOSTIC / LEARNER APPROVAL PRESERVED / RANGE NOT FORCED. POWO accepts Acer grandidentatum Nutt.; Acer saccharum subsp. grandidentatum and A. saccharum var. grandidentatum are homotypic synonyms, NOT proof this is the eastern A. saccharum concept. Texas state-native, notably Edwards Plateau canyons (NPSOT); no automatic 3-target-county PASS. LOOK HERE FIRST: simple opposite 3–5-lobed leaves with broad lobes and relatively shallower incisions; underside pubescent rather than the conspicuously silvery underside of A. saccharinum. USFS gives leaf blade 2.5–10 cm wide; paired samaras and young fruit can be hairy. Contrast silver maple's deep angular V-shaped sinuses, narrow pointed lobes and silvery lower surface. A. negundo has compound leaves, not simple palmately lobed leaves; ornamental A. palmatum is a cultivated/non-native comparison. CAUTION: samara pairs, opposite leaves and fall color are genus/overlapping cues, not species proof; leaf size, season, habitat alone unreliable. PHOTO ROLES: matched top/bottom leaf and sinus closeups with scale, abaxial hair macro, twig with opposite nodes, mature paired samaras, habitat secondary. Sources POWO https://powo.science.kew.org/taxon/1798-2 ; USFS https://research.fs.usda.gov/feis/species-reviews/acegra ; NPSOT https://www.npsot.org/posts/native-plant/acer-grandidentatum/
NON-NATIVE/CULTIVATED COMPARISON: Acer palmatum is Asian; all 3 project observations are cultivated. Exclude from native metrics.

rows.source_taxonomy_review: Reviewed 2026-10-07 | TAXONOMY+DIAGNOSTIC / LEARNER APPROVAL PRESERVED / RANGE NOT FORCED. POWO accepts Acer saccharinum L.; historic Acer dasycarpum is a synonym, not a second species. Texas native at state level; one iNat wild observation does not certify a project 3-county PASS. LOOK HERE FIRST: opposite simple leaves with 3–5 sharply pointed lobes divided by conspicuously DEEP, angular/V-shaped sinuses; underside silver-white/pale. Minnesota DNR reports leaf 4–6 in long and paired samaras 1–2 in long. Spring flowers typically emerge before leaf expansion and fruits mature in spring (supporting cue, not sole ID). Compare A. grandidentatum's broader less deeply cut lobes, pubescent rather than strikingly silver-white underside, and usually smaller canyon-tree habit; A. negundo has compound leaves. CAUTION: paired winged samaras, opposite nodes, general leaf lobing and bark are shared Acer features; cultivated vs wild origin is separate from species ID. PHOTO ROLES: same-scale adaxial/abaxial leaves and deep sinuses, samara pair with scale, spring bud/flower sequence, twig nodes; inspect user/Joey assets first. Sources POWO https://powo.science.kew.org/taxon/1892-2 ; MN DNR https://www.dnr.state.mn.us/trees/silver-maple.html ; UA https://arboretum.ua.edu/whats-growing-on/silver-maple-acer-saccharinum/

rows.source_taxonomy_review: Reviewed 2026-10-07 | TAXONOMY+DIAGNOSTIC / LEARNER APPROVAL PRESERVED / RANGE NOT FORCED. POWO accepts Allium canadense L.; the species includes multiple accepted varieties, so DO NOT silently assign var. canadense. Texas is native at state level; project 3-target-county PASS not evaluated. LOOK HERE FIRST: intact umbel spathe: FNA 3–4 bracts, 3–7-veined; umbel loose, 0–60 flowers, with flowering pedicels sometimes replaced by aerial bulbils. Var. canadense frequently has bulbils, BUT other varieties flower normally: bulbil absence is NOT an exclusion. Leaves 20–50 cm × 1–7 mm; scape 10–60 cm; pedicels 8–70 mm. Compare A. drummondii: 2–3 spathe bracts typically 1-veined, usually 10–25 flowers, bulbils rare, leaves 10–30 cm × 1–3(–5) mm, pedicels 5–20 mm. OVERLAP: pedicel lengths, leaf widths, white/pink tepals, onion odor, and umbel size; combine bract venation + reproductive architecture + leaf/scape proportions. PHOTO ROLES: same-scale umbel overview, opened spathe/veins macro, flowering vs bulbil-bearing umbel, leaf/base and bulb coat; inspect user/Joey assets first. FNA https://www.efloras.org/florataxon.aspx?flora_id=1&taxon_id=242101341 ; POWO https://powo.science.kew.org/taxon/527759-1

Reviewed 2026-10-07 | TAXONOMY+DIAGNOSTIC / LEARNER APPROVAL PRESERVED / RANGE NOT FORCED. POWO accepts Allium drummondii Regel; A. helleri, A. nuttallii and A. reticulatum var. nuttallii are synonyms, not extra learner species. Texas state-native; strict project 3-county PASS not evaluated. LOOK HERE FIRST: flowering umbel usually 10–25 flowers, bulbils rare; spathe 2–3 bracts, normally 1-veined (FNA); flowers campanulate to star-like 6–9 mm, tepals spread; scape 10–30 cm, leaves 10–30 cm × 1–3(–5) mm; pedicels 5–20 mm. Against A. canadense, prioritize spathe venation + umbel composition; A. canadense 3–4 3–7-veined spathe bracts, often bulbil-bearing but not always. CAUTION: pink/white tepals, onion odor, pedicel lengths and leaf widths overlap; do not key from flower color or no-bulbils alone. rows.source_taxonomy_review: Reviewed 2026-10-09 — accepted Anemone berlandieri Pritz. (POWO/FNA), Texas native at STATE level; project 3-target-county PASS NOT established. IMPORTANT HOMONYM: Anemone caroliniana Torr. & A.Gray (1838), an illegitimate later homonym, is a synonym of A. berlandieri; it is NOT the accepted A. caroliniana Walter (1788). LOOK HERE FIRST: one involucral-bract tier ABOVE midpoint of flowering scape; ALL basal leaves divided differently from bracts. Compare A. caroliniana (one tier below midpoint, one or more basal leaves similar to bracts) and A. edwardsiana (2 tiers). Color and sepal number overlap. PHOTO ROLES: entire scape with ruler and bract tier; basal leaf beside involucral bract; fruiting achene hair macro. Sources: https://powo.science.kew.org/taxon/urn:lsid:ipni.org:names:708260-1 ; https://efloras.org/florataxon.aspx?flora_id=1&taxon_id=101733

rows.source_taxonomy_review: Reviewed 2026-10-10 | Accepted Cyperus esculentus L. (POWO/FNA); native Texas at state level per POWO, strict 3-target-county PASS UNRESOLVED. Learner approval from Master Pool preserved; not canonical. LOOK HERE FIRST: dig for stolons and tubers, then dissect mature spikelets. FNA: soft/spongy flexible stolons when dried, tubers (3-)6-11 mm; flattened to compressed-quadrangular spikelets, persistent floral scales typically 1.8-2.7 mm (variable varieties), yellow-brown to brown. Distinguish C. rotundus: wiry hard stolons/tubers and often purplish-brown scales; color alone unreliable. Distinguish C. strigosus: cormlike basal swelling, deciduous scales, longer 3.2-4.5 mm scales. INFRASPECIFIC CAUTION: FNA recognizes var. leptostachyus, macrostachyus, heermannii; do not assign variety without mature spikelet measurements. PHOTO ROLES: excavated stolon/tuber paired macro, dried stolon texture, full umbel, flattened spikelet, floral scale with mm ruler, achene. Sources https://www.efloras.org/florataxon.aspx?flora_id=1&taxon_id=220003732 ; https://powo.science.kew.org/taxon/300668-2

Reviewed 2026-10-07 | TAXONOMY+DIAGNOSTIC / LEARNER APPROVAL PRESERVED / RANGE NOT FORCED. POWO accepts Acer grandidentatum Nutt.; Acer saccharum subsp. grandidentatum and A. saccharum var. grandidentatum are homotypic synonyms, NOT proof this is the eastern A. saccharum concept. Texas state-native, notably Edwards Plateau canyons (NPSOT); no automatic 3-target-county PASS. LOOK HERE FIRST: simple opposite 3–5-lobed leaves with broad lobes and relatively shallower incisions; underside pubescent rather than the conspicuously silvery underside of A. saccharinum. USFS gives leaf blade 2.5–10 cm wide; paired samaras and young fruit can be hairy. Contrast silver maple's deep angular V-shaped sinuses, narrow pointed lobes and silvery lower surface. A. negundo has compound leaves, not simple palmately lobed leaves; ornamental A. palmatum is a cultivated/non-native comparison. CAUTION: samara pairs, opposite leaves and fall color are genus/overlapping cues, not species proof; leaf size, season, habitat alone unreliable. PHOTO ROLES: matched top/bottom leaf and sinus closeups with scale, abaxial hair macro, twig with opposite nodes, mature paired samaras, habitat secondary. Sources POWO https://powo.science.kew.org/taxon/1798-2 ; USFS https://research.fs.usda.gov/feis/species-reviews/acegra ; NPSOT https://www.npsot.org/posts/native-plant/acer-grandidentatum/
